hints: Look carefully at which two pressure lines cross at each numbered point, for example at point 1 the dashed ventricle line crosses the dotted atrium line.

Remember valves are pushed open by a higher pressure behind them and slammed shut when pressure in front becomes higher, so compare ventricle vs atrium for the atrioventricular valve and ventricle vs aorta for the semilunar valve.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three lines**

First, use the key. The dotted line is the atrium (low pressure), the dashed line is the ventricle (big rise and fall), the solid line is the aorta (high pressure).

Valves only respond to pressure differences across them.

**Atrioventricular valve closes at point 1**

Just after 0.1 s, ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure as the ventricle starts to contract.

Higher pressure below pushes the atrioventricular valve shut to prevent backflow:
$$P_{ventricle} > P_{atrium} \rightarrow AV \text{ closes}$$

**Semilunar valve opens at point 2**

At about 0.15 s, ventricular pressure keeps rising and just exceeds aortic pressure.

Now blood can be pushed out into the aorta, so the semilunar valve opens:
$$P_{ventricle} > P_{aorta} \rightarrow \text{semilunar opens}$$

**Semilunar closes at 3, atrioventricular opens at 4**

At point 3 (about 0.4 s) ventricular pressure falls below aortic pressure, so the semilunar valve shuts to stop backflow from the aorta.

Just after, at point 4, ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure, so the atrioventricular valve opens and the ventricle can fill again. That gives 4, 2, 1, 3.

options.A: Incorrect. Point 1 is not AV opening, it is AV closing when ventricle pressure exceeds atrium pressure.
options.B: Incorrect. Point 2 is not AV opening, it is semilunar opening when ventricle pressure exceeds aorta pressure.
options.C: Incorrect. Point 3 is not AV opening, it is semilunar closing when ventricle pressure falls below aorta pressure.
options.D: Correct. Point 4 is AV opens, point 2 is semilunar opens, point 1 is AV closes, point 3 is semilunar closes.
